title: Is the Third Text a Weave of the Other Two
statement: Return `true` if the text `c` can be made by **weaving** the texts `a` and `b` together: take letters alternately from `a` and `b` in any pattern (several in a row from the same text is fine), but **keep the order of the letters inside each text**, and use every letter of both texts exactly once. For example `abxcy` is a weave of `abc` and `xy`.
constraints: a, b and c contain lowercase letters

examples.explanation: a, b from the first text, x from the second, c from the first, y from the second.
In `adbc` the d comes before the c, but in `cd` the c must come first.

hints.nudge: Look at the first i letters of a and the first j letters of b. They must together make the first i + j letters of c. What can the last letter of that prefix of c be?
hints.pattern: Dynamic programming over (i, j): ok[i][j] is true if the first i letters of a and the first j letters of b weave into the first i + j letters of c. It is true if the last letter of that prefix of c matches a[i - 1] and ok[i - 1][j], or matches b[j - 1] and ok[i][j - 1].
hints.pseudocode:
if len(a) + len(b) != len(c): return false
ok[0][0] = true
ok[i][j] = (i > 0 and ok[i - 1][j] and a[i - 1] == c[i + j - 1]) or (j > 0 and ok[i][j - 1] and b[j - 1] == c[i + j - 1])
return ok[len(a)][len(b)]
hints.walkthrough: Try all ways of assigning each letter of c to a or b and you get exponentially many cases, but the situation after reading i + j letters of c depends only on HOW MANY letters were taken from a (i) and from b (j). So tabulate ok[i][j]. The last letter c[i + j - 1] was taken either from a (then it must equal a[i - 1] and the prefixes (i - 1, j) must have worked) or from b (equal to b[j - 1] and (i, j - 1) worked). If the lengths do not add up the answer is false at once. Fill the table row by row; one row at a time is enough for the memory. O(len(a) * len(b)) time.
